title: Exact certificate excluding seven mutually unbiased bases in C^6 without Fourier vanishing (verifier and data)
description:
Standalone exact verifier and certificate data proving that there are no seven mutually unbiased bases in C6; by Weiner's gap theorem (Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 141 (2013) 1963–1969) this gives N(6) ≤ 5.

OpenAI's preprint Exact Fourier certificates for complex Hadamard matrices of order six (24 September 2026) proves the same bound in two parts: (A) the Matolcsi–Ruzsa–Weiner Fourier vanishing for every 6×6 complex Hadamard matrix except Tao's cubic one, with a separate exclusion of the cubic matrix; (B) a mixed-moment positivity certificate that uses the vanishing as an input. This deposit shows that part (A) is not needed: with the same six test-function lists and the same valid linear identities (contraction relations, order-one zeros, the second-moment/2-design identity, the mixed identities (36)–(37), symmetries), but without ever setting a moment to zero because a charge is a permutation of (1,1,1,−1,−1,−1), new positive definite integer Gram matrices give f = −821605927536823/38880, Σ|β| = 5531688869329/12960, f + Σ|β| < 0.

Contents: verify_d6.py (Python ≥ 3.8, standard library only; all certifying arithmetic is integer/rational; regenerates all relations), cert_d6_data.json (certificate data), SHA256SUMS, README.md, reference run logs (current verifier) and, in a subfolder, superseded logs of an earlier revision. Run: python3 -I verify_d6.py cert_d6_data.json (about 45–80 s depending on the machine, 0.4 GB). Assertions must be enabled; the verifier refuses to run under -O or PYTHONOPTIMIZE.
